intro: Register — choosing the word that fits the situation — is what separates sounding fluent from sounding foreign, and it works by levels, not by single words. Umgangssprachlich (chat, speech, character voice): kriegen, kaputt, klauen, checken, Kohle, gucken, sauer, ’ne Menge, kapieren, hinkriegen. Neutral (most writing and speech): bekommen, Geld, prüfen, beginnen, helfen, sagen, brauchen, sterben. Gehoben / formell (official letters, reports, obituaries): erhalten, entwenden, überprüfen, benötigen, verärgert, mitteilen, betrachten, bewerkstelligen, versterben, sich äußern. The formal word is usually longer, often Latinate or prefixed (be-, ver-, er-, ent-), and goes with nominal style; the colloquial one is short, Germanic, and goes with particles and contractions. At this stage you move between the three levels on demand and hear a shift in a text as a signal (irony, quotation, character voice). Neither level is ‘better’; the wrong one in the wrong place is the error — and mixing two levels in one sentence is the error native listeners hear first. This quiz gives you the colloquial sentence and the formal frame (or the reverse); you supply the word that fits the frame.
tips[0].title: Verbs: colloquial ↔ formal
tips[0].text: kriegen (ugs.) – bekommen (neutral) – erhalten (formell) · gucken – sehen – betrachten · anfangen – beginnen (both neutral; beginnen slightly more written) · helfen (neutral) – unterstützen, Beistand leisten (formell) · sagen – mitteilen, sich äußern · brauchen – benötigen · checken – prüfen – überprüfen · klauen – stehlen – entwenden · sterben – versterben · kapieren – verstehen – nachvollziehen · hinkriegen – schaffen – bewerkstelligen.
tips[0].check.why: Sie, beigefügte Unterlagen and Vollständigkeit set a formal frame, so you need the prefixed überprüfen; checken is colloquial and gucken means to look.
tips[1].title: Nouns and adjectives
tips[1].text: Kohle, Knete (ugs.) – Geld (neutral) – Mittel, Betrag (formell) · Job – Arbeit, Stelle – Tätigkeit, Position · Typ – Mann – Person, Mitarbeiter · ’ne Menge – viele – zahlreiche, erhebliche · kaputt – defekt · sauer – verärgert, ungehalten · echt gut – ausgezeichnet · riesig – beträchtlich · blöd – unklug, töricht.
tips[1].trap: versterben is only for people and only in formal contexts (obituaries, reports); 'der Hund ist verstorben' is comic. And erhalten replaces kriegen but not bekommen in 'Kinder bekommen' (to have children).
tips[1].check.why: In a formal report a person is der Mitarbeiter; Typ and Kerl are colloquial and clash with the nominal style around them.
tips[2].title: Three levels, and what each signals
tips[2].text: umgangssprachlich (kriegen, Kohle, checken): speech, chat, character voice. neutral (bekommen, Geld, prüfen, beginnen, helfen): most writing. gehoben / formell (erhalten, Mittel, überprüfen; versterben, sich begeben, gewahren): official, academic, literary. A sudden drop in level inside a formal text = irony or quotation.
tips[2].check.why: A sudden drop in register inside a formal text marks a quotation or irony; the writer does not adopt the phrase as their own.
tips[3].title: Longer, Latinate, prefixed = up; short, Germanic, particle-friendly = down
tips[3].text: erhalten / benötigen / überprüfen / zahlreiche vs kriegen / brauchen / checken / 'ne Menge. If you're unsure of a word's level, its length and its prefix usually tell you.
tips[3].check.why: genehmigen is the prefixed official verb; abnicken and durchwinken are colloquial images for approving something without much scrutiny.
remember[0]: Three levels: ugs. – neutral – formell; Geld and beginnen are neutral, Mittel and erhalten are formal.
remember[1]: Shift the whole sentence, not one word; a level drop inside a formal text is a signal.
mistakes[1].why: versterben is for people in formal register.
mistakes[2].why: One colloquial verb inside a formal sentence is the mix the raters hear first.
mistakes[3].why: Over-formal in an informal context is also a register error.
hook: Kriegen, bekommen, erhalten: learn to pick the word that fits a chat, an everyday email or an official letter.
recall.known: From "Register: informell → formell": du-chat to Sie-e-mail.
recall.today: Three levels per word (kriegen, bekommen, erhalten) and what each one signals.
tips[2].check.q: A sober news report says: Der Vorstand habe die Lage „voll im Griff“. What does the colloquial phrase in quotation marks signal?
tips[2].check.options[0]: The writer is quoting someone, probably with ironic distance
tips[2].check.options[2]: The phrase is the formal standard expression
tips[2].check.answer: The writer is quoting someone, probably with ironic distance
